solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sally's in favour of a stop in Torquay

parts.note: to be in favour of something is to be for it

indicators.note: the stop of a word is its end, so the final letter of Torquay is taken

explanation.surface: A person called Sally backs a break in the Devon resort of Torquay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name; it is the definition. Torquay is a seaside town in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden sortie or excursion, the same as a raid or venture out.

clue.text: Devotee acquires nothing in Paris — time for food?

parts.note: an enthusiast or fan is a nut, as in a fitness nut
the French word for nothing is rien

explanation.surface: A fan sits down to a meal in Paris, wondering if it's time to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that nourishes the body counts as nourishment; food is the general term for it.

clue.text: Encumbered without leader, and lost

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped, its leader being its head

parts.note: to be saddled with something is to be burdened by it

explanation.surface: Someone weighed down by responsibility, with no one to guide them, has lost their way.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled or confused, as when one's thinking has gone astray and is all at sea.

clue.text: Female on the George Washington possibly causes furore

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: the USS George Washington is a US Navy aircraft carrier, and USS (United States Ship) prefixes such vessels

explanation.surface: A woman aboard a US warship stirs up a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shows the George Washington is just one example of a ship named with the USS prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss and a furore are both an outburst of agitation or commotion.

clue.text: Fleeting sun brings out scanty wear

parts.note: something fleeting lasts only a short while, so is brief
S is the abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: A short burst of sunshine prompts people to put on skimpy clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpants or knickers are skimpy garments with little fabric, worn under other clothes.

clue.text: St Matthew's almost within easy reach –- it's huge!

parts.note: the apostle Matthew the tax collector is called Levi in the gospels of Mark and Luke
within easy reach is at hand, so these words give the first part of that phrase

indicators.note: the phrase loses its final letter, so it is not quite complete

parts.note: something in reach is to hand, the hand word supplying the rest

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how vast something near St Matthew's church is.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical sea monster, now any creature or thing of enormous size.

clue.text: Scan with a French instrument to reveal problem

parts.note: to con is to study or scan something closely
un is the French for a
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: Someone examines a French instrument to diagnose what is wrong with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or puzzling question, hard to resolve.

clue.text: In house, most exhausted, rain outside having departed

indicators.note: the letters of the rain word are removed from the outer parts of the longer word

parts.note: the most exhausted person is the weariest
rain is wet weather, so wet stands for it

explanation.surface: Indoors, the most worn-out person has the rain falling outside, now gone.
explanation.walkthrough: WE leaves the front and T the end of WEARIEST, the wet word split around the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology the sky is divided into twelve houses, the Ram being the first sign.

clue.text: Ebb with current in front

indicators.note: the current is placed inside the word for ebb

parts.note: to ebb is to fade or dwindle
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: The tide ebbs with a current running ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a building, or a false outward show presented to the world.

clue.text: Stall vehicle briefly but intermittently

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: taking letters on and off, every other one, from the word briefly

explanation.surface: A car stalls for a moment, then keeps cutting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' reads as a verb about engines; it is a noun, a booth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cubicle or booth in a library for private study, a kind of stall.

clue.text: Peaked cap dropped among swarming ants in hell-hole

indicators.note: the cap is put down into the middle of the jumbled letters
ants that swarm move about chaotically, so their letters are scrambled

parts.note: a kepi is a French military cap with a flat top and a peak

explanation.surface: A soldier's cap falls into a seething nest of ants, a nightmare place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peaked cap' is a single item, the French military kepi, not 'Peaked' as an adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit of serpents, and figuratively any place of chaos and danger, a hellish spot.

clue.text: Mariner — from HMS Beagle perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a beagle is a hound, so one aboard a ship would be a canine of the ocean, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A sailor who served on Darwin's ship, HMS Beagle.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced old sailor is a salty veteran of the ocean, a nautical old hand.

clue.text: For starters, gourmet rillettes including pheasant, emu and grouse

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so each word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A gourmet menu of starters: rillettes with pheasant and emu, plus grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like another game bird on the menu; it is a verb, the definition. Rillettes is a French potted-meat spread.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble or complain, the same as to moan.

clue.text: Estate agent's beginning to value in seconds

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word agent's is taken
the value word sits inside the two seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so seconds gives two of them
to set a price is to value something

explanation.surface: An estate agent starts valuing a property in a matter of seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the whole of their property and possessions, their holdings.

clue.text: Throw a wobbly as a 19 crashes

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the solution to 19 across, meaning spot on

explanation.surface: Someone has a tantrum as an exactly-right result falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for losing control and becoming wildly angry or excited.

clue.text: Marmite incorporates last of chowder that's left

indicators.note: the cooking vessel takes the extra letter into itself

parts.note: a marmite is a French earthenware cooking pot

indicators.note: the final letter of the word chowder

explanation.surface: A jar of the British yeast spread Marmite contains the dregs of some soup, which is all that remains.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British yeast-extract spread, but here it is the French pot it is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the left-hand side looking forward is called port.

clue.text: Wind blows in winter, interminably

indicators.note: letters blown about by the wind are scattered and rearranged
without its end, so the final letter of winter is removed

explanation.surface: A wintry wind blows on and on without ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' leaves WINTE, which 'blows' rearranges. 'Wind' is a verb here, rhyming with mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist or coil string around something, as when winding a ball of cord.

clue.text: 'Plain fish' medic's written in

indicators.note: the doctor's abbreviation is inserted into the fish

parts.note: a tuna is a large sea fish
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor jots 'plain fish' into a diet sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast treeless Arctic plain with frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Inadequate rest

definitions.meaning: to recline or prop oneself against something

explanation.definitionFit: Lean means both scanty, as in thin times, and to rest one's weight against a support.

clue.text: Particular gift from manager needing to be reduced?

definitions.meaning: a special strength or talent, from the card-game term for a suit one holds many cards in

definitions.text: from manager needing to be reduced?
definitions.meaning: an outfit worn by a boss that is too lengthy and must be shortened, read literally

explanation.surface: A special present from the boss needs scaling down.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, holding many cards of one kind is a strength, so the phrase means a forte.

clue.text: Strict prohibition surrounds group beyond state control

indicators.note: the prohibition word wraps around the organisation's initials

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
an NGO is a non-governmental organisation, independent of the state

explanation.surface: A tough ban is imposed around a group that operates outside government.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on or precise, exactly correct, which is a sense of strict or exact.

clue.text: Ageism, albeit evenly disseminated, can be a piercing thing

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, spread through the two words, are picked out

explanation.surface: Ageism, though fairly spread around, can wound people.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand tool with a screw tip for boring holes in wood.

clue.text: Small mammals settle away from three western parts

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so the first three letters go

parts.note: to settle a matter is to determine it

explanation.surface: Some little creatures move into a new home far from the western regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoats in their white winter coats, small mammals of the weasel family.

clue.text: Answer may appear in godsend some day

indicators.note: the letter turns up inside the godsend word

parts.note: manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites, so a godsend

explanation.surface: The answer to one's prayers may arrive like a gift from heaven someday.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for tomorrow, used to mean at some unspecified later time.

clue.text: Low note in brass

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of a cow, to moo
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A deep note played on a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' suggests a band instrument; it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang words for money or cash.

clue.text: Boot out from Liberal Democrats, without discreet negotiation

indicators.note: the letters of the second word are taken away from the first
what is left is negotiated, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem is kicked out of the party without any quiet talks.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DISCREET's letters from LIBERAL DEMOCRATS leaves letters that rearrange to the answer. The Liberal Democrats are a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of laced ankle boot named after the royal castle in Scotland.

clue.text: Engine off the rails

definitions.meaning: short for locomotive, a railway engine

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as a shortening for a railway engine and as slang for being crazy.

clue.text: Native returning Sioux's greeting — but he won't be there!

indicators.note: the word for native is read backwards

parts.note: a native son is someone born in a place
how is the greeting attributed to the Sioux in old westerns

explanation.surface: A Sioux greets a returning native, though someone will be missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who books but fails to turn up is an absentee.

clue.text: Roll around in horrible gabardine

indicators.note: the letters found are turned around and read the other way
the letters lie inside the words horrible gabardine

explanation.surface: Someone rolls about in an awful raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds LEGAB inside 'horrible gabardine'; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Trace special constable — at home prior to Arsenal's kick-off

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer police officer
to be in is to be at home
till means until, before a time

indicators.note: the start of the word, so its first letter

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer stays home until Arsenal's football match kicks off.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; a special constable is a part-time volunteer police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or spark, the merest hint of something.
